::: {.why}
This is the single most useful thing your statistics training buys you in this field, and almost nobody in it reports the interval.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Derive the asymptotic standard error of an estimated Sharpe ratio under iid returns, using the delta method.
- Say how many years of daily data are needed before a true Sharpe of 1 is distinguishable from 0 at conventional confidence.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>55 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Derive it. The estimator is the ratio of the sample mean to the sample standard deviation. Write the joint asymptotic distribution of those two moments under iid normal returns, apply the delta method, and simplify. You should land on a variance of the form one plus half the squared Sharpe, divided by the sample size.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Check the derivation by simulation rather than by trusting the algebra: generate 10,000 return series with a known true Sharpe at your sample length, compute the realised Sharpe for each, and compare the empirical standard deviation against your formula. They should agree to two decimal places.
:::
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Three years of daily returns, realised Sharpe 1.0. Give the standard error and say whether you can reject a true Sharpe of zero.
:::
